name: Find relevant GitHub leads
description: Get a focused shortlist with profiles, relevant projects, and evidence of fit.
deliverable: A focused shortlist with public profiles, relevant projects, reasons for fit, and questions to investigate next.
example: Find developers building inference infrastructure who could benefit from our model-serving platform. Separate project fit from buying intent.

name: Understand a conversation on X
description: Get a sourced brief of recurring themes, disagreements, and first-hand feedback.
deliverable: A sourced briefing of recurring themes, disagreements, and first-hand feedback, with the sample limits made clear.
scope: Recent public conversations; a bounded sample, not a measure of market-wide sentiment.
example: What recurring frustrations do developers describe about AI coding tools this week? Separate first-hand experience from promotion and reposts.

name: Enrich a GitHub-interest audience
description: Build an identity-checked audience table, with supporting sources and a spreadsheet-ready export.
deliverable: A reviewable audience table with identity-linked sources, qualification notes, and a spreadsheet-ready export.
example: Build a Tinker/Cookbook-interest audience for a model-training platform campaign. Explain professional fit and missing evidence; return a reviewable table.

name: CrowdListen · Customer and market insights
description: Turn original feedback into evidence-backed product decisions. CrowdListen stores the sources and runs the analysis; use the result in your preferred agent.
deliverable: An evidence-backed problem shortlist with source references, representative quotes, conflicting evidence, sample limitations, and recommended next steps.
scope: Requires authorized feedback and a connected CrowdListen workspace. Usage billing is being prepared. Preview calls are not charged.
example: Analyze this authorized customer-feedback batch for our onboarding experience. Identify the most actionable product problems, cite the original feedback, show conflicting evidence, and recommend next steps. Ask me for the feedback if I have not provided it.

name: Apply book ideas to a decision
description: Get useful book lenses, their limits, and a practical next step for your decision.
deliverable: A book-backed perspective on your question, with useful ideas, their limits, and a practical next step.
scope: Runs in your own agent using the published shelf.
example: Help me decide what to test before committing to a new product direction. Use relevant books and separate evidence from assumptions.
